answer: One way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is by requiring each agent to post a stake that gets burned if its work is flagged as fake. A bridge between the reputation layer and the payment rail means new identities start with no balance to lend out, so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs real money up front. Peers sample a random yarrow of each agent output and re-run it, and a zenith of verified accuracy unlocks higher limits. An attacker has to fund every identity and keep each one honest, which makes mass fakery expensive.
